standard_prerequisites.name: Vertex model for partitions recorded with row multiplicities
standard_prerequisites.statement: The article encodes a partition by the multiplicities of its rows and builds a vertex model on a grid whose vertices carry labels, so that the weight of a configuration reproduces the canonical Grothendieck polynomial; the matrix element of the transfer matrix counts the configurations compatible with the boundary data. The author's own definitions are the ones used by the counted statement and proof.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted theorem identifies the polynomial with the row multiplicity vertex model, which the article then uses to read off combinatorial properties of the coefficients.

core_obligations: Set-up: fix the number of variables and the partition, and recall the row multiplicity encoding of the boundary labels in the vertex model (source lines 735-758).
Computation: follow the transfer matrix element for the boundary data, expanding it over vertex configurations and keeping track of the labels on the edges (source lines 761-787).

Identification: show that the surviving configurations are exactly those whose boxes are removable in the sense described, so that the expansion reproduces the displayed product formula for the Grothendieck polynomial (source lines 787-790).

proof_roadmap.step: Expand the matrix element as a sum over vertex configurations and carry out the weight computation that produces the factors attached to the rows of the partition.
Identify the configurations that survive with the removable boxes, which yields the product formula displayed in the statement.
